steps.name: principal
steps.claim: ctx.Doer is used as the issue poster and actor for this request.

steps.name: request_form
steps.claim: The parsed CreateIssueOption supplies title, body, ref, deadline, milestone, assignees, labels, projects, and requested closed state.

steps.name: check_deadline_issue_write
steps.claim: The handler checks issues-unit write permission only to decide whether to accept the requested deadline.

steps.name: deadline_choice
steps.claim: A deadline is copied only when one was supplied and issues-unit write permission is present; otherwise the zero deadline remains.

steps.name: set_deadline
steps.claim: The requested deadline is placed on the issue candidate.

steps.name: continue_after_deadline
steps.claim: Continue constructing the issue candidate.

steps.name: leave_deadline_zero
steps.claim: The issue candidate keeps the zero deadline when the deadline condition is not met.

steps.name: continue_without_deadline
steps.claim: Continue constructing the issue candidate.

steps.name: issue_candidate
steps.claim: The handler constructs an issue candidate for repository with principal as poster and request title/body/ref.

steps.name: check_option_issue_write
steps.claim: The handler checks issues-unit write permission to decide whether milestone, assignees, and labels may be supplied.

steps.name: writer_option_choice
steps.claim: Writers may request milestone and assignees; non-writers have labels cleared and proceed toward NewIssue rather than being denied creation.

steps.name: set_milestone
steps.claim: The requested milestone is placed on the issue candidate.

steps.name: resolve_assignees
steps.claim: Requested assignee names are resolved to IDs and may fail before creation.

steps.name: validate_assignability
steps.claim: Each resolved assignee is checked for assignability to the repository; a missing, inaccessible, or operationally failing assignee prevents creation.

steps.name: assignee_validation_choice
steps.claim: Creation continues only if assignee resolution and validation complete successfully.

steps.name: clear_labels
steps.claim: When issues-unit write permission is absent, all requested labels are cleared.

steps.name: create_without_writer_options
steps.claim: The non-writer path still invokes NewIssue with the issue candidate, cleared labels, no assignees, and requested projects.

steps.name: reader_creation_result
steps.claim: NewIssue success reaches post-creation handling; blocked-user, permission/not-exist, and other errors abort the request.

steps.name: create_with_writer_options
steps.claim: The writer path invokes NewIssue with requested permitted metadata after assignee validation.

steps.name: writer_creation_result
steps.claim: NewIssue success reaches post-creation handling; any returned error aborts the request.

steps.name: reject_invalid_assignee
steps.claim: Assignee resolution, lookup, or assignability failure returns an API error before NewIssue.

steps.name: reject_new_issue_error
steps.claim: NewIssue errors abort creation; blocked users receive forbidden, permission-denied/not-exist errors receive bad request, and other errors receive an internal error.

steps.name: issue_creation_completed
steps.claim: A successful NewIssue call has created the issue candidate in the selected repository.

steps.name: requested_close_choice
steps.claim: If the request asks for Closed, the handler attempts a separate post-creation CloseIssue operation; failure can yield an error after creation.

steps.name: close_created_issue
steps.claim: The handler calls CloseIssue for a requested initially closed issue; dependency or operational errors can stop the response after creation.

steps.name: close_result
steps.claim: A close error returns an API error, while success proceeds to the created response.

steps.name: reject_after_creation
steps.claim: CloseIssue failure returns an error even though NewIssue already succeeded.

steps.name: created_response
steps.claim: The handler refetches the issue and returns HTTP 201 if refetch succeeds; refetch failure returns an internal error after creation.

# Security Report Format

Use this template for all `/security-review` output. Generated during Step 7.

---

## Report Structure

### Header
```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║           🔐 SECURITY REVIEW REPORT                     ║
║           Generated by: /security-review skill          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

Project: <project name or path>
Scan Date: <today's date>
Scope: <files/directories scanned>
Languages Detected: <list>
Frameworks Detected: <list>
```

---

### Executive Summary Table

Always show this first — at a glance overview:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           FINDINGS SUMMARY                     │
├──────────────┬──────────────────────────────── ┤
│ 🔴 CRITICAL  │  <n> findings                  │
│ 🟠 HIGH      │  <n> findings                  │
│ 🟡 MEDIUM    │  <n> findings                  │
│ 🔵 LOW       │  <n> findings                  │
│ ⚪ INFO      │  <n> findings                  │
├──────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┤
│ TOTAL        │  <n> findings                  │
└──────────────┴─────────────────────────────────┘

Dependency Audit: <n> vulnerable packages found
Secrets Scan: <n> exposed credentials found
```

---

### Findings (Grouped by Category)

For EACH finding, use this card format:

```
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[SEVERITY EMOJI] [SEVERITY] — [VULNERABILITY TYPE]
Confidence: HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📍 Location:  src/routes/users.js, Line 47

🔍 Vulnerable Code:
  const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${req.params.id}`;
  db.execute(query);

⚠️  Risk:
  An attacker can manipulate the `id` parameter to execute arbitrary
  SQL commands, potentially dumping the entire database, bypassing
  authentication, or deleting data.

  Example attack: GET /users/1 OR 1=1--

✅ Recommended Fix:
  Use parameterized queries:

  const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?';
  db.execute(query, [req.params.id]);

📚 Reference: OWASP A03:2021 – Injection
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
```

---

### Dependency Audit Section

```
📦 DEPENDENCY AUDIT
══════════════════

🟠 HIGH — lodash@4.17.20 (package.json)
  CVE-2021-23337: Prototype pollution via zipObjectDeep()
  Fix: npm install lodash@4.17.21

🟡 MEDIUM — axios@0.27.2 (package.json)
  CVE-2023-45857: CSRF via withCredentials
  Fix: npm install axios@1.6.0

⚪ INFO — express@4.18.2
  No known CVEs. Current version is 4.19.2 — consider updating.
```

---

### Secrets Scan Section

```
🔑 SECRETS & EXPOSURE SCAN
═══════════════════════════

🔴 CRITICAL — Hardcoded API Key
  File: src/config/database.js, Line 12
  
  Found: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY = "sk_live_FAKE_KEY_..."
  
  Action Required:
  1. Rotate this key IMMEDIATELY at https://dashboard.stripe.com
  2. Remove from source code
  3. Add to .env file and load via process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
  4. Add .env to .gitignore
  5. Audit git history — key may be in previous commits:
     git log --all -p | grep "sk_live_"
     Use git-filter-repo or BFG to purge from history if found.
```

---

### Patch Proposals Section

Only include for CRITICAL and HIGH findings:

````
🛠️  PATCH PROPOSALS
══════════════════
⚠️  REVIEW EACH PATCH BEFORE APPLYING — Nothing has been changed yet.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
Patch 1/3: SQL Injection in src/routes/users.js
─────────────────────────────────────────────

BEFORE (vulnerable):
```js
// Line 47
const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${req.params.id}`;
db.execute(query);
```

AFTER (fixed):
```js
// Line 47 — Fixed: Use parameterized query to prevent SQL injection
const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?';
db.execute(query, [req.params.id]);
```

Apply this patch? (Review first — AI-generated patches may need adjustment)
─────────────────────────────────────────────
````

---

### Footer

```
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

📋 SCAN COVERAGE
  Files scanned:     <n>
  Lines analyzed:    <n>
  Scan duration:     <time>

⚡ NEXT STEPS
  1. Address all CRITICAL findings immediately
  2. Schedule HIGH findings for current sprint
  3. Add MEDIUM/LOW to your security backlog
  4. Set up automated re-scanning in CI/CD pipelines

💡 NOTE: This is a static analysis scan. It does not execute your
   application and cannot detect all runtime vulnerabilities. Pair
   with dynamic testing (DAST) for comprehensive coverage.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

---

## Confidence Ratings Guide

Apply to every finding:

| Confidence | When to Use |
|------------|-------------|
| **HIGH** | Vulnerability is unambiguous. Sanitization is clearly absent. Exploitable as-is. |
| **MEDIUM** | Vulnerability likely exists but depends on runtime context, config, or call path the agent couldn't fully trace. |
| **LOW** | Suspicious pattern detected but could be a false positive. Flag for human review. |

Never omit confidence — it helps developers prioritize their review effort.

answers.explanation: Source behavior does not enforce the supplied policy. POST /repos/{username}/{reponame}/issues requires a token, a non-archived repository, successful request binding, and reqRepoReader(unit.TypeIssues), not an issues-unit writer guard. reqRepoReader admits a principal with issues-unit read permission and also has repository-admin and site-admin exceptions. repoAssignment selects the repository, computes ctx.Repo.Permission for ctx.Doer (or no access when enforced 2FA is unmet), requires some unit/public access, and checks token access. Inside CreateIssue, CanWrite(unit.TypeIssues) is a genuine write-level test because CanWrite returns CanAccess(AccessModeWrite, unitType), but the handler uses it only to restrict metadata: without write permission it omits the deadline and milestone/assignees and clears requested labels, then still calls issue_service.NewIssue. The service checks blocked-user conditions and invokes the model creation transaction; the model allocates an issue index and inserts the issue into the selected repository. No issues-unit write check is visible in that service/model chain. Therefore an authenticated principal admitted by the reader route can create a basic issue without issues-unit write permission, subject to the other route, token, repository, blocked-user, validation, and operation-success conditions. A principal with issues-unit write permission is also admitted and may additionally supply the guarded metadata. Repository-admin and site-admin admission are relevant route exceptions and must not be conflated with read permission itself. A requested initial Closed state and the post-creation refetch can fail after NewIssue has already succeeded, so an error response can occur after the creation effect.

paths.explanation: For the source-visible successful path, an authenticated caller that passes reqToken, repository/token assignment checks, mustNotBeArchived, binding, and reqRepoReader(unit.TypeIssues) reaches CreateIssue. If CanWrite(unit.TypeIssues) is false, the handler strips writer-only metadata but still delegates to NewIssue; successful model insertion creates the issue in ctx.Repo.Repository. If CanWrite is true, creation likewise proceeds with additional permitted metadata. Operational errors can deny completion, and post-creation close/refetch errors can occur after insertion.

policy.text: Creating an issue requires write permission to the repository's issues unit. Read permission to the repository alone does not authorize this write.

counterfactuals.explanation: If the route used an issues-unit writer guard, or CreateIssue/NewIssue rejected when CanWrite(unit.TypeIssues) was false, the read-only case would be denied and would conform to the supplied policy. This revision instead continues to the creation call after removing privileged metadata.

answers.explanation: The source-visible successful path allows basic issue creation without issues-unit write permission. POST /repos/{username}/{reponame}/issues applies reqToken, mustNotBeArchived, request binding, and reqRepoReader(unit.TypeIssues), rather than a writer guard. reqRepoReader accepts issues-unit readers and separately admits repository administrators and site administrators. repoAssignment selects ctx.Repo.Repository, computes ctx.Repo.Permission for ctx.Doer (or no access when enforced 2FA is unmet), requires some unit/public access, and checks token access. CreateIssue calls CanWrite(unit.TypeIssues), which is a write-level check because CanWrite returns CanAccess(AccessModeWrite, unitType), but uses the result to control metadata rather than the basic creation effect: without write permission it omits writer-only deadline, milestone, and assignee handling and clears labels, then still calls issue_service.NewIssue. That service checks blocked-user conditions and calls the model NewIssue transaction; the model allocates an index and inserts the issue into the selected repository. No compensating issues-unit write check is visible in the reviewed service/model chain. A principal with issues-unit write permission follows the same creation path and may additionally provide guarded metadata. Relevant exceptions and conditions include repository-admin/site-admin route admission, token and repository visibility/access checks, enforced 2FA, archived repositories, blocked-user relations, validation and database errors, and optional post-creation close/refetch failures. In particular, CloseIssue or refetch may fail after NewIssue has already created the issue, so an error response does not necessarily mean the protected effect did not occur.

paths.explanation: An authenticated principal that passes token, repository assignment/access, non-archived, binding, and reqRepoReader(unit.TypeIssues) checks can reach CreateIssue. When CanWrite(unit.TypeIssues) is false, the handler strips or omits privileged metadata but still calls NewIssue; successful model insertion creates the basic issue in ctx.Repo.Repository. When CanWrite is true, creation is likewise allowed with additional guarded metadata.

policy.text: Creating an issue requires write permission to the repository's issues unit. Read permission to the repository alone does not authorize this write.

counterfactuals.explanation: If the POST route required an issues-unit writer guard, or CreateIssue/NewIssue rejected the false CanWrite(unit.TypeIssues) branch before insertion, the read-only case would be denied as the supplied policy requires.
